name: Pilatus PC-12 / U-28 Draco
summary: Best-selling single-engine business turboprop, used by PlaneSense, Boutique Air and air ambulances; AFSOC flies it as the U-28A Draco ISR aircraft.

wings: Low, straight, long-span wing with upturned winglets
engines: Single PT6A turboprop with a four- or five-blade propeller
Exhaust stacks on both sides of the cowling
fuselage: Long fuselage with large rectangular windows
Large cargo door on the left rear fuselage
U-28A: gray paint, belly sensor turret and many antennas
tail: T-tail with a small swept horizontal stabilizer
Tall swept fin with a dorsal fillet

tellTales: Winglets on a long straight low wing
Big cargo door on the left rear fuselage

confusedWith.howToTell: The PC-12 has a T-tail and winglets on a long wing; the TBM has a conventional low tail and a stubbier fuselage.
The PC-12 is much larger with a T-tail; the PA-46 is a small low-tail single with a slim fuselage.
The PC-12 has a low wing and retractable gear; the Kodiak has a strut-braced high wing and fixed gear.
The PC-12 has a low wing, T-tail and retractable gear; the Caravan has a strut-braced high wing, low tail and fixed gear.
The Epic has a smooth, tapered composite fuselage, large oval windows and a low tailplane; the PC-12 has a T-tail and a boxy, slab-sided fuselage.
